title: Scalar compatibility of the direct general-ring orientation
statement: Let D, ell, X, Y, f, d, n, A satisfy the following hypotheses: D is the global algebraically closed finite-field datum; ell is prime and different from its characteristic; X and Y are separated schemes of finite type over D.k; f is a separated D.k-morphism smooth of pure relative dimension d; n>=1; and A is a finite commutative ring killed by ell^n, and supply Noetherian structures, quasi-compactness and one compactification of f. Put P equal to the bottom Q_ell setting of [def-sp-general-ring-canonical-data]. There are a unital prime-ring identification e, a scalar/root-generator normalized coefficient-line comparison t, a direct ordinary dualizing orientation alpha, and actual smooth diagonal geometry G. The canonical dualizing-unit map u is invertible, as is the scalar exceptional comparison c; their maps satisfy c u^{-1} nu^*(alpha) = the prescribed scalar extension of P.diagonalDualizingObject. Alpha satisfies OrientationNormalized for G. This asserts the orientation clauses only and asserts neither the tensor formula nor exponent independence.

source.place: Proof (1) and (2): scalar coefficient comparison and the direct diagonal/Rees/integration orientation

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$. The unital structure map $R\to A$ exists because $\ell^nA=0$. Use the fixed coefficient-independent compactification supplied by [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] for $f$ at both coefficient rings. The unit $R_Y$ is in the bounded constructible finite-Tor category (it is free of rank one in degree zero). Thus [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] gives $c_f:(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{f,A}$. Apply [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] at $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, whose level-$n$ quotient is exactly $R$, to obtain $\theta_{f,R}:\omega_{f,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}R_X(d)[2d]$. All its scheme hypotheses hold in our explicit separated finite-type setting. Since $\ell$ is invertible on every $k$-scheme here, the Tate clause applies. By the free-line and exact-functor clauses of [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor], scalar extension carries this isomorphism to $(\omega_{f,R})_A\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d]$. Set $\theta_{f,A}^{(n)}=(\theta_{f,R})_A c_f^{-1}$. This proves clause (1), with exactly its displayed map and arrow directions.

We compare the three arrows in the diagonal/DNC construction, rather than infer canonicity from the existence of an isomorphism. Put $W=X\times_YX$, with $p_1,p_2$ and $\Delta$. The prime-power diagonal arrow $a_R:C_R(p_1,\Delta)\to\omega_{f,R}$ is the base-change identification of [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change]. Its construction uses the smooth base-change exchange and $p_2\Delta=1_X$. The base-change and pullback coherence in [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport], applied with $g_0=f$, $h=f$, and $g'_0=p_1$ to this square (the base-change clause requires no section of $f$), gives
$$a_A q_{p_1,\Delta}=c_f(a_R)_A.$$
Here $a_A$ is the same specified base-change composite over $A$, not an arbitrary identification. For the actual normal bundle $\pi_N:N_\Delta\to X$, the normalized deformation map $\delta_R:C_R(p_1,\Delta)\to C_R(\pi_N,0_N)$ is [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. The final equation of [lem-pur-dnc-coefficient-transport] gives
$$\delta_A q_{p_1,\Delta}=q_{\pi_N,0_N}(\delta_R)_A.$$
That lemma identifies $\delta_A$ with the direct normalized construction over $A$, and supplies its uniqueness at $t=1$. The pair is eligible: the diagonal of the smooth separated map $f$ is a closed section of $p_1$ and its actual normal bundle is the rank-$d$ tangent bundle, as stated in [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. The geometry, including this bundle, is the same at both coefficient rings. The helper uses [def-pur-dnc-section-family] for that geometric space and its structural maps; its two displayed formulas define the family objects separately at $R$ and $A$, so the fixed-coefficient convention of that definition is respected.

The last arrow $\beta_R:C_R(\pi_N,0_N)\to R_X(d)[2d]$ is the zero-section pullback of the canonical vector-bundle orientation [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. More precisely, at $R$ the theorem [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] explicitly specifies its inverse as the transpose of the inverse projection formula followed by integration $t_{\pi_N}$; this is the integration normalization specified in our statement. Over a trivializing open, vector integration is the affine-space counit, and [def-amb-vector-integration] specifies it for every finite ring, including $A$, by these local restrictions and unique gluing. Let $T_D=D_N(d)[2d]$ and let $j_D:T_D\to\omega_{\pi_N,D}$ be the adjoint transpose of $t_{\pi_N,D}$ for $D=R,A$. The specified affine trace of [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] is the counit of the ordered affine-space adjunction, so on a trivializing open $j_D$ is the identity in that adjunction's identification $\omega_{p_d,D}=D(d)[2d]$. The chart clause of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] uses the counit-preserving chart identification, with counit the fibre sum followed by the specified affine-space counit. On a vector-bundle trivializing open the etale coordinate map is the identity, so this fibre sum is the identity and it identifies $c_{\pi_N}$ with the coefficient identification between precisely these affine right adjoints; thus on that open $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A=j_A$. To pass from charts to global maps, $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A:T_A\to\omega_{\pi_N,A}$ is an isomorphism, since $j_R$ and $c_{\pi_N}$ are isomorphisms. Its target is therefore a locally free rank-one sheaf shifted by $[2d]$, as is its source. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful], after removing that common shift both $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A$ and $j_A$ are ordinary sheaf morphisms. Their equality on each trivializing open gives equality globally by [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing]. Thus $c_{\pi_N}(j_R)_A=j_A$. The left-hand map is invertible, so $j_A$ is invertible and $j_A^{-1}c_{\pi_N}=(j_R^{-1})_A$. Restrict along the zero section and use the pullback/tensor identification [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] and the free-line identification [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. This gives the pullback of the equality between the specified inverse-integration maps just proved. In the pro-etale realization the same equality holds: by [lem-pur-finite-ring-site-tensor-transpose](3), applied to $\pi_N$ with $M=D_N(d)[2d]$, $K=D_X$ and $e=t_{\pi_N,D}$ for $D=R,A$, the pro-etale transpose of the transported integration is $\nu^*$ of the etale $j_D$ under the counit-preserving identification $\rho$ of its clause (1); the chart counits of [det-sp-reduction-exceptional] are transported from the etale site through the same comparison, and the tensor comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Consequently the last arrow of the direct $A$-construction satisfies
$$\beta_A q_{\pi_N,0_N}=(\beta_R)_A.$$
The coefficient notation at the zero section is canonical by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. This argument concerns specified integration and its transpose; it never asserts that all isomorphisms of Tate lines coincide.

theorem finiteGeneralRingOrientation
    (D : WeilConjectures.FiniteFieldDatum.{u})
    (ell : ℕ) [Fact ell.Prime] (hEll : ell ≠ D.p)
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of D.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of D.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f] [HasCompactification f]
    (d : ℕ) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f]
    (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (hA : ((ell ^ n : ℕ) : A) = 0) :
    let P := finiteGeneralRingPrimeSetting D ell hEll n hn
    let hAU := congrArg (fun a : A ↦ (⟨a⟩ : ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) hA
    ∃ e : P.Ring ≃+* ULift.{u} (ZMod P.diagonalExponent),
    ∃ t : Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.CoefficientLineComparison
        (RingHom.ulift.{u + 1, u + 1, u, u} (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e))
        P.diagonalExponent P.diagonalExponent P.diagonalExponent_annihilates hAU X,
    ∃ alpha : Etale.dualizingComplex (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)) f ≅
        Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.line (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) P.diagonalExponent hAU X d,
    ∃ geometry : Etale.FiniteRingSectionDeformation.Geometry d
        (pullback.fst f f) (pullback.diagonal f),
    ∃ hunit : IsIso (finiteGeneralRingDualizingUnitMap (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) f),
      IsIso (finiteGeneralRingReduction P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e) f) ∧
      finiteGeneralRingReduction P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e) f ≫
          @inv _ _ _ _ (finiteGeneralRingDualizingUnitMap (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) f) hunit ≫
          (Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.comparison (ULift.{u + 1, u} A) X).map alpha.hom =
        (finiteGeneralRingOrientationExtension P (finiteGeneralRingCoefficientMap P A hA e)
          hAU d f (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k)) t).hom ∧
      Etale.FiniteSmoothPurity.OrientationNormalized (ULift.{u + 1, u} A)
        P.diagonalExponent (pow_pos P.coefficients.prime.out.pos P.level)
        hAU f d geometry (P.diagonalExponent_isUnit (f ≫ (Y ↘ Spec (.of D.k)))) alpha
